column1: # GH#19 S6 (task #120) — PINNED PRODUCTION ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA for saw/invSaw anti-aliasing
# in the continuous wave-morph ring, and for the dynamic-PWM reference convergence.
# This file is the EXPECTATION. tools/gh19_s6_saw_acceptance.py reads it and never writes it. As in
# S3, two independently produced artifacts are cross-checked against it, so neither the criteria nor
# a run can quietly shrink the matrix:
#   * the probe's own declared stimulus plan (gh19_s6_plan.tsv), written by the probe from its
#     compiled-in axes BEFORE the first render, and
#   * the `axis` rows below, from which the gate RE-DERIVES the required cell set and requires it to
# A cell deleted from an enumeration, or an axis edited to shrink the product, makes the two
# disagree and the gate REFUSES instead of accepting a smaller matrix.
# THE TWO CRITERION FAMILIES ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE, AND WHY (this is the S6 correction).
# The morph ring renders  y = (1-u) * node_k(p) + u * node_{k+1}(p)  on each stretch. On stretch 0
# (saw -> invSaw) the naive mixture's true jump at the phase wrap is
# and its peak amplitude is |1 - 2u|. BOTH vanish together at u = 0.5, i.e. norm = 0.125: there the
# mixture is identically zero for every phase (0.5*saw + 0.5*(-saw) == 0).
# That single fact splits the matrix in two, and it is why the anti-phase midpoint CANNOT be an
#   * IMPROVEMENT cells  -- positions where the uncorrected arm genuinely jumps, so "at least 6 dB
#     of residual reduction versus the preserved uncorrected baseline" is a well-posed, satisfiable
#     demand. Required: every one of the 120 improvement cells clears BOTH residual thresholds.
#   * EQUALITY cells     -- the two positions where an improvement threshold is UNSATISFIABLE and
#       - norm = 0.125 (u = 0.5): amplitude 0 AND jump 0, so the baseline residual is already ~0 and
#         the correct arm's residual is ~0 too. A 6 dB criterion here would be RED for a CORRECT
#         implementation: it measures nothing, it only fails.
#       - norm = 0.5 (the SINE node, u = 1 on stretch 1): the naive waveform is already smooth, so
#         there is no jump to remove and no improvement to demand. The invariant that DOES hold
#         exactly is that the new correction terms have coefficient 0 there, so the default output
#         must be BIT-IDENTICAL to the SAME BUILD with those two terms neutralised (arm A vs arm B,
#         one compiler, one set of flags). See the head of this file's criterion block: the
#         comparison is an A/B and not a comparison against the committed pre-S6 snapshot, because
#         a snapshot rendered by another libm cannot be reproduced bit-for-bit from this one.
#     These are asserted as equalities, not thresholds. Putting them in the improvement group would
#     have been a degenerate-identity error: two arms that are both identically zero (or both
#     already smooth) cannot be told apart by a ratio of their residuals.
# WHY THE A/B ALONE IS NOT ENOUGH, AND WHAT THE `wiring` ROWS ADD. An A/B at morph 0.5 shows that
# the correction does not reach the DEFAULT patch. It cannot show that the correction has no other
# reachable caller: the two terms could be applied on some path the A/B never renders, and arm A
# and arm B would still agree on the eight windows. The `wiring` rows below therefore DECLARE, as
# code-hit counts per file and name, where the six symbols S6 introduces are referenced at all, and
# the gate requires the declaration to equal the tree (an undeclared caller, a moved count, or a
# vanished symbol is a FAIL naming the file, the line and the identifier). Together the two layers
# cover the whole claim: the A/B covers "the correction changes nothing at the default node", the
# wiring declaration covers "the correction is reachable only from the one guard block, and only
# WHY THE MIDPOINT IS STILL IN THE MATRIX AT ALL. It is a necessary-but-insufficient REGRESSION
# guard, and it is cheap: it catches leakage of a correction that should be absent. It does NOT
# discriminate "correct per-node weight scaling" from "copy the kernel unscaled", because the
# unscaled arm also evaluates to 0 there and the naive arm was 0 anyway. The discriminating power
# for that question lives entirely OFF-centre (norm 0.0625 / 0.1875 / 0.3125 / 0.375 / 0.4375) --
# see the NC1 negative control, which is built on those cells and not on the midpoint. No cell in
# this file is asked to do more than it can.
# WHERE A SIGN ERROR IS ACTUALLY CAUGHT (amended after the mutant matrix was measured, not before).
# This file previously said the midpoint row "catches a SIGN error". The measurement says otherwise,
# and the row's role is restated here to match the evidence rather than the intent:
#   * A sign error (`invsaw-sign-flip`: the invSaw term added with the wrong sign) is caught by the
#     ANALYZER'S ALIGNMENT LICENSE, at the midpoint's own degenerate branch: the pre-S6 law is
#     identically 0 there, so the license demands the candidate be exactly 0 and refuses the arm --
#     align_bad = 8, and the 8 refused cells ARE the morph-0.125 set (named by id, not merely
#     counted). That refusal happens a layer BEFORE this gate: an unlicensed arm produces no report
#   * `EQUALITY-ANTIPHASE` therefore exists as a SECOND-LINE assertion and is STRUCTURALLY
#     UNREACHABLE from the product side: any mutation that would make it fire makes the midpoint
#     non-zero, and that is exactly what the license's degenerate branch refuses first. It is kept
#     because the gate is a standalone artifact that can be run against a report it did not render,
#     and its reachability is demonstrated there (gate-only synthetic input; NOT a product negative
#     control; not counted as a mutant arm). No threshold or cell membership is changed by this
#     amendment -- only which surface is credited with catching what.
#   * The same layer ordering explains the DC guard: `GUARD-DC`'s quantity is also fed by the
#     report, and a product-wide additive offset is refused by the license on all 168 cells before
#     the gate sees it. Its reachability is demonstrated the same way.
#   * It explains the frequency guard too, which was measured AFTER this amendment was first
#     written and is the reason the paragraph says "three" rather than "two": `phase-drift` (the
#     rendered step changed by 2%) is refused by the license on 160 of the 168 cells. The 8 that
#     survive are the exact-zero midpoint cells, and they survive for a reason worth stating -- the
#     license's degenerate branch asks only `0 == 0`, which a changed step cannot disturb. So the
#     same 8 cells that cannot discriminate a sign error cannot witness a frequency fault either;
#     a cell carrying no signal there cannot report on what happened to the signal. `GUARD-FREQ`
#     is fed by the PROBE's own zero-crossing column rather than by the report, so its gate-side
#     reachability demonstration aims at that column instead (same label: gate-only synthetic
#     input, not a product negative control, not counted as a mutant arm). No threshold or cell
#     membership is changed by this amendment.
# THRESHOLDS. Each improvement cell must clear BOTH residual thresholds against the PRESERVED
# UNCORRECTED baseline, with the same fixed reference, phase and denominator, no re-fitting and no
# threshold change. The guard rows are the ways an improvement can be faked; they are checked on the
# same cells, in the same pass. Columns and their derivations are inherited unchanged from S3, so a
# reader who checked the S3 numbers can check these.
# `report` rows are quantities the gate MUST emit and MUST NOT judge. A `report` row the gate fails
# to emit is a REFUSAL, so "reported separately" cannot quietly become "not reported".
# REFERENCE FAMILY ATTRIBUTION (S3's lesson, applied). Each cell's reference is constructed from
# THAT CELL'S OWN mix law: on stretch 0 the reference is (1-u)*bl_saw + u*bl_invSaw with
# bl_saw = sum_{k=1..kmax} -2/(pi*k) * sin(2*pi*k*p) and bl_invSaw = -bl_saw (exact), and on
# stretch 1 it is (1-u)*bl_invSaw + u*bl_sine with bl_sine = sin(2*pi*p) (exact), each truncated at
# kmax = floor(sr/2/f0). A single-waveform model is NOT the model of a mixed cell, so no reference
# is borrowed across stretches or across families; the u=0 and u=1 limits are asserted in the
# analyzer's --self-check, which is what keeps this a second reference rather than a second guess.
# THE `axis`/`axis_set` ROWS DRIVE THE RECONCILIATION. S6's cell set is a UNION of two
# cross-products (the A layer over three frequencies, the B layer over one), so it is declared as
# two `axis_set` groups; the gate derives each group's product separately and requires
#   {cell rows} == (product of axis_set A) U (product of axis_set B)
# with no cell in both. The equality group is reconciled the same way against axis_set EQ.
# report_only_cell rows: positions the probe renders and the report covers, but which are in NEITHER
# gated group (the high-frequency set, past the point where a two-point step kernel has a
# band-limited referent). They are pinned so the plan reconciliation stays EXACT:
#   plan_static == {cell rows} U {equality_cell rows} U {report_only_cell rows}
# A cell that disappears from one group cannot be absorbed by another: the equation fails.
# Equality criteria. Tolerance is exact (0.0); these are identities, not measurements, so
# there is no level bound to derive and none is claimed.
# `sine_node_bit_diff_count` is a SAME-BUILD A/B and NOT a comparison against a committed
# snapshot: the gate is given `--cand-arm` (arm A: this tree's product, both S6 correction terms in
# force) and `--neutral-arm` (arm B: the same source with those two terms neutralised by
# tools/stage_gh19_s6_shadow.py, same compiler, same flags), and requires the eight default
# sine-node windows to agree bit for bit. The criterion, the threshold (0) and the claim are
# unchanged from the original -- "at the sine node the two correction terms have coefficient 0, so
# the default output does not move" -- but the second side is now produced by THIS run instead of
# read from the committed pre-S6 arm.
# WHY IT HAD TO CHANGE. The committed baseline was rendered on macOS. The default patch evaluates
# `std::sin(kTwoPi * p)`, Apple's libm and glibc disagree by exactly 1 ULP on 3.76% of identical
# arguments, and the criterion therefore read 0 locally and 652 on the CI toolchain -- the same 652
# that a literal pre-S6 tree produces there, i.e. the gap is the toolchain and not the change.
# Measured, not reasoned: see report/2026-09-25-task120-gh19-s6-morph-aa.md, which is where the
# four compiler/platform pits this project has hit (C4996, C3493, C4723, and this sin-ULP one) are
# ARM B MUST BE NON-VACUOUS. If the neutralisation failed to take effect, B would BE A and the
# identity would hold trivially. The gate therefore refuses (code NEUTRAL-ARM, not a failure) when
# the two arms' plan files differ, when a witness window cannot be read, or when the arms are
# identical on the morph-0.0 witness cells -- the saw node, where the two terms ARE in force and
# therefore where A and B must visibly differ.
# `wiring <file> <symbol> <code-hit-count>`: where the six symbols S6 introduces are REFERENCED in
# the product, as code hits (comments and the contents of string/char literals blanked before
# counting, so a symbol named in a comment or a static_assert message is not a caller). The gate
# requires these declarations to equal the tree in BOTH directions -- a hit not declared, a declared
# hit that is gone, a count that moved, a symbol with no declaration line, or a region other than
# the guard block referencing the three corrected names is FAIL S6-WIRING, naming file, line and
# identifier. A file that cannot be read is REFUSE WIRING-SOURCE instead: that is an input problem,
# and no judgement about the product follows from it. Scanned roots: core, host, generated.
# A DECLARATION IS ITSELF A CODE HIT, which is why most rows are not 1. In vco.h the two
# `*BlepWeight_` methods and `sawJumpResidual_` each count 2: their definition plus their one read
# (`sawBlepWeight_` / `invSawBlepWeight_` are bound at 310/311 immediately above the guard, and
# `sawJumpResidual_` is called at 313 inside it). The two wave_map weights count 1 each in vco.h --
# the read inside the corresponding `*BlepWeight_` body (369, 382) -- and `nodeWeight` counts 0
# there at all: it is only ever reached through the two named weights. In vco_wave_map.h `nodeWeight`
# counts 3 (declaration at 283, called at 296 and 305 by sawWeight and invSawWeight), the other two
# named weights count 1 each (their declarations at 294 and 303), and the three `_` symbols count 0:
# the correction's kernel is a Vco member and is not reachable from the wave-map header.
# Axis groups. A = the 9-point grid reduced to the positions with a genuine uncorrected
# jump, three frequencies; B = the remaining off-centre positions, one frequency. The
# frequency dimension is NOT cut: every A-layer position keeps all three.
